clue.text: See 24
See 28
Hurry to take in very busy area

indicators.note: the word for hurry takes the abbreviation into its middle

parts.note: to hie is an old word for to hurry

explanation.surface: An instruction to rush and fit something into a frantic place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hive of activity is a proverbially bustling place, so a busy area fits.

clue.text: Coastal site? Overlooking it on a ship

indicators.note: to overlook is to leave out, so the two-letter word is dropped from the word site

parts.note: taken as written, the word site before the deletion
taken as written, the two letters removed
aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: A seaside spot, and someone gazing at it from the deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' looks like a view over the water but means ignoring: SITE without IT leaves SE. The question mark makes 'Coastal site' look like the definition, but 'site' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for land bordering the ocean is used attributively, as in seaboard towns, meaning by the coast.

clue.text: Hang about — Cockney's grabbed some money after turning

indicators.note: the combination is turned round to read the other way
a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: held means grabbed
a wad is a bundle of banknotes

explanation.surface: A Londoner loiters after pocketing a bit of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney traditionally drops initial H, so 'Cockney's grabbed' is HELD without its H; 'after turning' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang about is to linger idly and waste time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Finish course for intending politicians in French city

parts.note: to die is to finish or come to an end
PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is the Oxford degree famously taken by would-be politicians

explanation.surface: Completing a degree for future politicians while living in France.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is an Oxford degree course whose graduates include many British politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a Channel port in Normandy, an example of a French city.

clue.text: Encouraged to follow one in German car, up in London suburb

indicators.note: the word for encouraged comes after the car part
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
the numeral goes inside the car's name

parts.note: BMW is the German car maker
I is the Roman numeral one
led on means encouraged or egged on

explanation.surface: Someone egged on to tail a numbered German car heading north into London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside BMW to give BMIW; 'up' reverses that to WIMB, and LED ON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon is a district of south-west London, home of the tennis championships.

clue.text: Collapse of valiant European

indicators.note: a collapse knocks the letters of valiant into a new heap

explanation.surface: A brave European falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapse of' rearranges VALIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Latvia, a Baltic state, is one kind of European.

clue.text: Lighten a line with float (not first time)

indicators.note: only the earlier of the two occurrences of the time letter is dropped

parts.note: to levitate is to float in the air

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a fishing line lighter by adding a float.
explanation.walkthrough: LEVITATE has two Ts; 'not first time' removes the first, giving LEVIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or relieve a burden is to make it lighter, so lighten is a synonym.

clue.text: Comeuppance for the pharmacist?

parts.note: the idiom for being treated as you treat others, taken literally for someone who dispenses drugs

explanation.surface: A druggist finally getting what they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for suffering the treatment you dish out is read literally: a chemist swallowing their own prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means receiving the same unpleasant treatment one has given others, which is a comeuppance.

clue.text: Gravitas not originally recalled in representative phrase

indicators.note: called back, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: bottom can mean substance or solidity of character

explanation.surface: Seriousness that was not there at first is remembered in a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not originally' drops the B of BOTTOM, leaving OTTOM; 'recalled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short saying adopted to represent a family, school or organisation.

clue.text: See 8
Has zero successes, having ignored Independent

parts.note: O looks like zero

indicators.note: the word for successes leaves out the letter for Independent

parts.note: wins are successes

explanation.surface: A sportsman with no victories, having been overlooked by this newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so has is a direct synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Company weathered slump — one having active drive

indicators.note: worn by the weather, so the word slump is battered into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on means working or active

explanation.surface: A firm survived an economic downturn, with one employee showing energetic ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weathered' rearranges SLUMP to MPULS.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsion is an irresistible urge, a kind of inner drive.

clue.text: Stop ignoring Conservative, accommodating revolutionary blue with little difficulty

indicators.note: the shortened word for stop holds the turned-round word for blue inside it
the word for stop leaves out the abbreviation for Conservative

parts.note: to cease is to stop

indicators.note: revolving the word for blue reverses its letters

parts.note: racy means risqué or blue

explanation.surface: A political call to stop ignoring the Tories and let in some radical blue thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' here means risqué, not Tory colour; 'revolutionary' turns that word round, giving YCAR, and 'accommodating' houses it in EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or fabric labelled as such needs little effort to look after, so is managed without trouble.

clue.text: Concern about deity's lumbering steed

indicators.note: the word for concern goes round the god's possessive

parts.note: care is concern
Thor is the Norse god of thunder; with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Worry over a god's slow, heavy horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught horse bred for hauling is a ponderous, plodding kind of steed.

clue.text: Noted steps taken with this in support

definitions.text: Noted steps taken with this in support

parts.words: Noted steps taken with this in support
parts.note: steps set to music are performed on this surface

explanation.surface: Musical footwork performed with something holding it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes, not remarked upon; the support is what the dancers stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance floor is the surface laid down for dancing, supporting those performing steps to music.

clue.text: Each tin possibly containing a brew

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the A within
the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Every tin may hold a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges EACH TIN to CHINTEA; 'containing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea from China, such as lapsang souchong, is a type of drink that is brewed.

clue.text: See 15
Collection of works of writer involved in music

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

indicators.note: the writing tool is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: MUS is the abbreviation for music
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: An anthology by a novelist who dabbles in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' gives O, as in o'clock: a convention the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology gathering several works, often by one author, in one volume.

clue.text: Has vaguely accepted meaning attached to one Oriental city

indicators.note: the numeral is joined on at the end
the jumbled letters take in the word for meaning
done vaguely, the letters of has lose their order

parts.note: hang means meaning or gist, as in getting the hang of something
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone half-grasped the significance of a single Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' turns the clue's first word into SHA, and 'accepted' slots the word for meaning in after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is the great port city of eastern China, in the Orient.

clue.text: He left beloved one? That's extremely significant

parts.note: luv is a casual spelling of love, a term for a beloved
a means one

explanation.surface: A man abandoned his sweetheart, which matters enormously.
explanation.walkthrough: LUV is the informal British form of address 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang intensifier means 'a hell of a', describing something very great or remarkable.

clue.text: Extravagant friends?

parts.note: pals are friends; the word slap, read upwards in this down light, spells pals

explanation.surface: Lavish companions?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the first part read 'up' (backwards) gives PALS, which is what 'friends' means.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, lavishly generous feast, so the word means extravagant.

clue.text: Laid-back number note discussion about computer network

indicators.note: the word for discussion goes around the network

parts.note: a chat is a discussion
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A relaxed exchange about the office network.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calm and unconcerned is relaxed, the informal sense of laid-back.

clue.text: Vital Bishop should exert grip on French cathedral city

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer tightly between them

explanation.surface: A key churchman ought to keep control of a French diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should exert grip on' shows the answer gripped inside 'vitAL BIshop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albi in southern France is famous for its brick cathedral of Sainte-Cécile.

clue.text: Amongst things to see, mark new events for men

indicators.note: the mark and new letter are placed among the letters of the word for things to see

parts.note: sights are things worth seeing
a tag is a mark or label

explanation.surface: Tourist attractions featuring a fresh mark for male occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: These are parties for a groom-to-be before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: These pre-wedding parties for a bridegroom and his male friends are events for men.

clue.text: Not easily moved? About to be upset after sign of grief

indicators.note: the sign of grief is placed first, with the turned letters coming after it

parts.note: a sob shows grief

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the two letters are reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone stoical whose composure gives way after shedding a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sober person is calm and steady, not easily stirred by emotion (or by drink).

clue.text: Measure of pressure to be put stormily around it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the two-letter word
a storm throws the letters about

explanation.surface: A barometric gauge gets put in place during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormily' rearranges TO BE PUT to POTTUBE; 'around' puts IT after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pitot tube is an instrument measuring fluid pressure, used for airspeed in aircraft.

clue.text: Son, having cracked beer record, is no longer conscious

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word for beer

parts.note: ale is beer
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A young man who broke a drinking record has passed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping has lost awareness, so is not conscious any more.

clue.text: Seeing a sandal drifting in Mediterranean area

indicators.note: drifting letters float out of their order

explanation.surface: Spotting a sandal floating off somewhere in the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' rearranges SEEING A SANDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: These Greek islands, such as the Cyclades, lie in a part of the Mediterranean Sea.
